images.caption:
How excited I was when I went to the Boti Falls, one of the most spectacular waterfalls in Ghana! Students of  our institute MASTECH ADVANCE INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY could not hide their joy when they visited Boti Falls in the Eastern Region of Ghana day before yesterday.
The excursion was organized by the institute administration on the 11th of April 2014. Before the journey began at about 8.0AM, staffs ensured that all necessary arrangement were executed before the bus took off. Students were very comfortable in the air-conditioned bus. They were also entertained with an action movie in the moving bus.
Even though vehicular traffic on the road made us to move at a snails pace, the entire drive is uphill, as the falls are located in an elevated village, so the drive was beautiful. We drove into the hills that Somanya looks onto, we arrived at the fall by 11.30 AM. We paid a fee to get in (2 Cedis for nationals and 10 Cedis for expats like me), and then 5 Cedis for a guide. We weren’t sure if we would need the guide initially, but, after our experience with one, We would definitely recommend it. The guides know the area like the back of their hand and provide some neat historical information along the way.Our guide informed us that we had to visit the umbrella rock and the three branched palm tree.
The trek to the umbrella rock was very difficult. In order to get to umbrella rock, we had to hike up a mountain. The guide called it Stubborn Mountain. At first, I didn’t really understand why, but after we reached the second portion of the hike, I felt like the “stubborn” description was an understatement. The mountain is entirely rough rock, covered in dirt which makes the climb a slippery one. At some points, I felt like I am looking straight up at the rock I am about to climb and I rested on the trees along the pathway to help me up. Passing through the jungle to the rock made the trip even more exciting as this was my trekking experience. Check out the pictures I took below. 
After hiking up the mountain, we finally reached umbrella rock. The sweaty walk was worth it. Umbrella rock is literally a giant natural rock that overlooks the Ghanaian hills.. When we arrived at the site,  I couldn’t believe my eyes. How could such a big rock be held in place for a long time without tumbling down? I asked myself. Some of our students decided to climb to the apex for a group picture, I didn’t dare.
There are people who live at the top of the mountain as well. They live off of the land around umbrella rock and also make a small living from the tourists who want to climb the ladders on top of the rock or climb the three-headed palm tree. They sell water sachets (purified water in a bag, a popular way of drinking water here) and goodies along the way for tired travelers.
After spending some time under and on top of the rock, our guide urged us to move to the three branched palm tree. We were all amazed at the site of the tree. Most of the students did not waste time in taking pictures. I was not left out.
We then made our way back down Stubborn Mountain. Descending back to the reception, we all took packaged lunch and then my eyes were keen to catch the sight of the falls from the hillside. Finally, we were on our way to the final part of our adventure – Boti Falls. I was so excited to finally see the natural wonder. It was a enchanting beauty. Majority of the student darted down the hillside straight to the falls.
By the time I got to the fall, most students had removed their clothes and were swimming and having a nice time in the water, swam until the guide informed us it was time to go.I felt like jumping out of my skin to feel the cold Boti water, and could not resist myself to go knee deep water for few snaps at the fall.
At about 5.30PM we were all seated in our luxurious bus and departed back to the institute. The Boti falls is really an interesting place to visit.

Last but not the least, all these were possible because of my stubborn daring hubby with whom I wish to encounter my fear and face any challenge in life. I would encourage all who visit Ghana to make it a point to visit Boti falls.
